messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] quantile fail in epi package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Using Epi 0.6 trying to stat.table a single quantile value (I want other
than 0.5 in other circumstances) I get

> stat.table(list(decade,Sex),quantile(Ggt,probs=c(0.5)),data=ggt)

Error in quantile(Ggt, probs = c(0.5)) : The quantile function only accepts
scalar prob values within stat.table

> stat.table(list(decade,Sex),quantile(Ggt,probs=0.5),data=ggt)

Error in quantile(Ggt, probs = 0.5) : The quantile function only accepts
scalar prob values within stat.table

 

looking at source I see

quantile <- function(x, probs, na.rm=TRUE,names=TRUE,type=7,...) {

if (length(probs > 1))

stop("The quantile function only accepts scalar prob values within

stat.table")

tapply(x, INDEX=subindex, FUN = stats::quantile, probs=prob,

na.rm=na.rm,names=names,type=type,...

and wonder if 

if (length(probs > 1))

stop("The quantile function only accepts scalar prob values within

stat.table")

 

should be

if (length(probs) > 1)

stop("The quantile function only accepts scalar prob values within

stat.table")

?

I don't know about using R source so haven't tested it.

Or am I doing something else wrong?

Note that:

> names(ggt)

[1] "labno" "date" "time" "Relrec" "Age" "DOB"

[7] "Sex" "CC" "RefDoctor" "Lab" "Na" "K"

[13] "Cl" "CO2" "Ag" "Glu" "Ur" "creat"

[19] "Urate" "Tbil" "Cbil" "Alkp" "Ggt" "Alt"

[25] "Ast" "Ld" "Ca" "Corca" "Phos" "Tprot"

[31] "Alb" "Glob" "Iron" "Chol" "Trig" "Fast"

[37] "coldate" "DOBdate" "agey" "decade" 

> 

so I think the 

quantile(Ggt, part should be OK.

Regards

Nigel
